pharm: Platinum-based alkylating agent that forms intra- and inter-strand DNA crosslinks, inhibiting DNA replication
quick: Single agent 360 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 4 weeks, or AUC-based (Calvert formula)
Can cause fetal harm (embryotoxic and teratogenic); avoid in pregnancy
Reduce initial dose in renal impairment; clearance correlates with CrCl
No specific adjustment established; use with caution
No specific interaction; general caution in ill patients
CBC with differential and platelets, renal function, electrolytes, audiology, neuro exam
summary: Carboplatin is a second-generation platinum coordination antineoplastic used primarily for advanced ovarian carcinoma, alone or in combination with other agents. It produces DNA crosslinks that inhibit replication. Compared with cisplatin it causes less nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and emesis but more myelosuppression. It carries a boxed warning for dose-related bone marrow suppression and anaphylactic-like reactions.
indications: Initial treatment of advanced ovarian carcinoma in established combination with other approved chemotherapeutic agents (e.g., with cyclophosphamide)
Palliative (secondary) treatment of patients with advanced ovarian carcinoma recurrent after prior chemotherapy, including patients previously treated with cisplatin

dosage.d: 360 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 4 weeks; do not repeat courses until neutrophils are at least 2,000 and platelets at least 100,000
dosage.t: Infuse intravenously; do not use aluminium-containing needles or sets
dosage.n: Alternatively dose by the Calvert (AUC) formula

dosage.d: Carboplatin 300 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 4 weeks for 6 cycles, with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 IV day 1 every 4 weeks
dosage.t: Intravenous infusion on day 1 of each cycle
dosage.n: Do not repeat until neutrophils at least 2,000 and platelets at least 100,000
Used to individualize dose by renal function; total dose is in mg, not mg/m2

dosage.d: Reduce initial dose: baseline CrCl 41-59 mL/min give 250 mg/m2; CrCl 16-40 mL/min give 200 mg/m2 on day 1 every 4 weeks
dosage.n: Adjust subsequent doses by blood count nadirs

admin: Administer under supervision of a physician experienced in cytotoxic chemotherapy with facilities for managing complications
Do not use needles or intravenous administration sets containing aluminium parts, which react with carboplatin causing precipitate and loss of potency
Obtain peripheral blood counts before each course and verify recovery before repeating
Use appropriate antiemetic premedication; emesis is a frequent effect
Be prepared to manage anaphylactic-like reactions with epinephrine, corticosteroids, and antihistamines
moa: Carboplatin is a platinum coordination compound that acts as an alkylating agent. It produces predominantly intrastrand DNA crosslinks (and some interstrand crosslinks), interfering with DNA replication and transcription in a cell-cycle non-specific manner, leading to cytotoxicity. Its biochemical activity is similar to that of cisplatin.

absolute: History of severe allergic reactions to cisplatin or other platinum-containing compounds
relative: Renal impairment (require dose reduction and close monitoring)
Concomitant nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs such as aminoglycosides
Prior cytotoxic or radiation therapy (increased myelosuppression)
monitor: Complete blood counts during and between courses
Renal function (serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, BUN)
Serum electrolytes including sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium

preg: Carboplatin can cause fetal harm. It is embryotoxic and teratogenic in rats given the drug during organogenesis (historically Pregnancy Category D). Avoid use in pregnancy; if used or if the patient becomes pregnant, advise of the potential hazard to the fetus. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception.
lact: It is not known whether carboplatin is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, discontinue breastfeeding during treatment with carboplatin.
renal: Carboplatin clearance correlates with the glomerular filtration rate, and renal impairment markedly increases drug exposure and myelosuppression. Reduce the initial dose in patients with reduced creatinine clearance (CrCl 41-59 mL/min: 250 mg/m2; CrCl 16-40 mL/min: 200 mg/m2) and adjust subsequent doses by the observed blood count nadirs. AUC-based (Calvert) dosing incorporates GFR.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment for hepatic impairment is established. Carboplatin undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism; use with general caution and monitor for cumulative toxicity.

major: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy or radiation (additive bone marrow suppression)
moderate: Live vaccines (risk of disseminated infection during immunosuppression)
Phenytoin (chemotherapy may reduce phenytoin absorption and levels)
minor: Drugs causing additive nausea may worsen emesis
interactions.food: Not applicable; carboplatin is administered intravenously
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; general caution in debilitated patients
interactions.diagnostics: May cause electrolyte disturbances (low sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium) and abnormal liver and renal function tests

common: Electrolyte abnormalities (low Na, K, Ca, Mg)
serious: Severe dose-related bone marrow suppression with infection or bleeding
emergency: Anaphylactic-like reaction (rash, flushing, dyspnea, hypotension, bronchospasm within minutes) - stop infusion and treat with epinephrine, corticosteroids, and antihistamines
Febrile neutropenia or severe bleeding - seek emergency care

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelets before each course and weekly until recovery (nadir around day 21)
Serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, and BUN
Serum electrolytes including sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium
Audiometry and neurologic examination, especially with cumulative dosing or prior cisplatin
Signs of hypersensitivity during and after infusion
counsel: This medicine is given by a healthcare professional into a vein; keep all appointments for blood tests
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bleeding or bruising, which may signal low blood counts
Report any rash, itching, facial swelling, or trouble breathing during or after infusion immediately
Use effective contraception; the drug can harm an unborn baby, and breastfeeding should be stopped
Report numbness, tingling, hearing changes, or persistent nausea and vomiting
pk: Cytotoxic effect develops over the treatment cycle; nadir counts around day 21
Peak plasma platinum at end of intravenous infusion
Initial plasma elimination half-life about 1.1-2 hours; total platinum is long
Dosing repeated every 4 weeks; myelosuppression cumulative
Store vials at 25 C (77 F) with excursions 15-30 C; protect from light; do not refrigerate
pearls: Boxed warning: dose-related bone marrow suppression (can be severe, causing infection or bleeding) and anaphylactic-like reactions that may occur within minutes of administration
Causes more myelosuppression but less nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and emesis than cisplatin
AUC (Calvert) dosing individualizes the dose by renal function and reduces toxicity
Never use aluminium-containing needles or IV sets - aluminium inactivates carboplatin
Thrombocytopenia is often the dose-limiting toxicity; nadir around day 21
missed: Carboplatin is administered on a scheduled cycle by a healthcare professional. If an appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; do not attempt to make up doses at home. Courses are not repeated until blood counts have adequately recovered.
overdose: There is no established antidote for carboplatin overdose. Anticipated complications are severe myelosuppression, hepatic and renal toxicity, and ototoxicity. Management is supportive with blood product transfusions, antibiotics for febrile neutropenia, and growth factor support. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
